ESSAY:
Exercise is good for you. It makes you fit and helps you not to be fat. Fit people can run and jump good. When people run, they feel happy. Exercise is also good for your heart and can make you live longer. If you don’t do exercise, you might be sad, and that’s bad. Sometimes, people go to gyms, but that is boring. It costs money too. You can just walk outside or play a game. Playing games is fun and also exercise. You can do exercise by dancing or whatever you like. It helps you look good which makes others like you more. A good thing about exercise is that it helps you sleep good. Sleeping well is very important because if you don't sleep well, you will be tired in the morning. If you do exercise every day, your body will be strong and you will not get sick. Exercise helps your brain too because it makes you think better. So, in conclusion, exercise is important and everyone should do it a lot.

ESSAY:
Social media is bad and it have a impact on people's lives. Many people spend too much time on social media like Facebook, Twitter and Instagram. This can lead to problems like not talking to real friends and family. People just stare at their phones and forget about real life. Also, social media can make people feel sad or jealous because they see others having fun. Adults and kids both can get bullied online and it hurts. 

Also, people think they can say anything on social media and it’s okay. But it’s not, because sometimes people get in trouble for what they write. There are also bad things like fake news that spread quickly, and it’s hard to know what is true or not. 

In conclusion, social media can have a negative effect. People need to be careful because it can make them less happy, and they don’t talk to people in person anymore. 

They should spend more time with their friends and family and less time on social media.

ESSAY:
The debate on whether university education should be free is complex. On one hand, education is a right, and every person should have access to it regardless of their financial situation. Free university could lead to more educated citizens, which is beneficial for society as a whole. If everyone could go to university without the burden of tuition fees, more people might pursue higher education and contribute positively to the economy. 

On the other hand, critics argue that having free education would put a financial strain on the government. It would require a lot of funding and could lead to higher taxes. Moreover, if everyone goes to university, there might be an oversupply of graduates, causing degrees to lose their value. 

Also, people often appreciate and value more what they pay for. If education is free, it could lead some students to take it less seriously. In conclusion, while there are significant advantages to making university education free, there are also valid concerns that need to be considered, making it a challenging issue.

ESSAY:
Renewable energy is becoming increasingly vital in the fight against climate change and the depletion of natural resources. Unlike fossil fuels, which are finite and contribute to greenhouse gas emissions, renewable energy sources such as solar, wind, and hydroelectric power offer cleaner alternatives that can be replenished naturally. Investing in renewable energy not only helps reduce our carbon footprint but also promotes energy independence, reducing reliance on imported fuels.

Moreover, the transition to renewable energy can drive economic growth by creating jobs in manufacturing, installation, and maintenance of renewable technologies. As demand for clean energy solutions rises, so too does the need for a skilled workforce, which can stimulate local economies and provide sustainable employment opportunities.

Additionally, renewable energy can contribute to energy security by diversifying our energy sources. With the instability of oil markets and geopolitical tensions, incorporating renewables into our energy mix can provide a more stable and resilient energy infrastructure.

In conclusion, the importance of renewable energy cannot be overstated. It presents an opportunity not only to combat climate change but also to invigorate economies and ensure a sustainable future for generations to come. Embracing renewable energy is not just an environmental imperative, but a pathway toward an economically viable and energy-secure world.

ESSAY:
Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative force in society, impacting various aspects of our daily lives and changing the way we interact with technology. One significant role of AI is its ability to process vast amounts of data, enabling organizations to make informed decisions quickly and efficiently. In sectors like healthcare, AI algorithms analyze patient data to provide personalized treatment plans, thereby improving patient outcomes.

Moreover, AI enhances productivity across industries by automating mundane tasks, allowing human workers to focus on more creative and strategic endeavors. For instance, in manufacturing, AI-driven robots streamline production lines, which can lead to increased efficiency and reduced costs.

However, while AI holds immense potential, it also raises ethical concerns. Issues regarding privacy, job displacement, and algorithmic bias prompt critical discussions about the responsible integration of AI systems. It is essential for policymakers, technologists, and society at large to collaborate in shaping frameworks that ensure AI technologies are developed and used ethically.

In conclusion, AI plays a crucial role in advancing societal capabilities, but it demands careful oversight to maximize benefits while minimizing potential harms.
